editionLabel: Rio Grande Games English rules, ©2020, twenty-page Exhibition Guidelines
firstPlayerRule: The person the group considers the best artist starts. If that cannot be decided, the rules let the players choose another selection method.
clarifications: Play proceeds clockwise. Use this order when distributing the numbered Starting Gold cards during setup.
The rulebook supplies no test or scoring system for artistic ability. Its permission to choose another method is official.
location: Setup step 9; Sequence of Play; final credits
evidence: Read setup and turn context; visually inspected title, setup, turn sequence and credits. Printed copyright is 2020, not the PDF URL's 2021 directory. Discovery used a retailer's link to the publisher-hosted PDF; the guessed publisher product page returned 404 and is not cited as provenance.
uncertainty: Artistic ability has no prescribed measurement; the official alternative handles an unresolved choice.
poolReason: A subjective opening-player criterion with an official alternative; selecting the person requires no components.

editionLabel: Helvetiq English rules, undated two-page sheet with Coiledspring Games UK importer
firstPlayerRule: Whoever visited a museum most recently starts the first raid.
houseFallback: If the visit is tied or nobody has visited a museum, agree to choose randomly. This is this site's suggested house rule.
clarifications: Later raids start with the player holding the Guard Dog figure; the museum criterion selects only the opening player.
The Alibi comparison breaks a final-score tie. It does not decide who starts.
location: How to Play on the first sheet; End of a Raid and End of the Game on the reverse
evidence: Both publisher PDF sheets were read and visually inspected. The opening visit criterion and later Guard Dog priority are separate. No publication year is printed in the inspected sheet.
poolReason: The opening criterion is portable; later component-based round priority stays in the clarification.

editionLabel: SPIEL DAS! / IELLO German rules, ©2023, v1 file; English summary
clarifications: The chosen player takes the first bidding-or-passing turn in the property-buying phase. Turns proceed clockwise.
In later buying rounds, the winner of the preceding auction starts. House selection and reveal in the selling phase are simultaneous.
location: Spielvorbereitung step 4; Spielablauf; buying-round end; selling phase; final credits
evidence: Rechecked the cached German publisher/distributor PDF and all five listed renders. The English IELLO PDF's text corroborates the initial rule but is not substituted for this edition.
poolReason: A random-only instruction provides no different selection criterion for the random-rule mix.

editionLabel: Pegasus Spiele German rules, ©2024, version 1.0; English summary
clarifications: Players then alternate turns, starting by playing a Clan card.
In the Clanfehde multi-round variant, the players alternate who starts each round.
The rulebook does not define how close to Scotland a visit must be.
location: Spielvorbereitung step 4; Spielablauf; Clanfehde variant; final credits
evidence: Rechecked all four listed rendered pages. The German instruction explicitly includes Scotland or somewhere nearby. Printed credits identify ©2024 Pegasus/IELLO and v1.0. Clanfehde's alternating later-round starter is not a previous-winner criterion.
poolReason: An opening-player travel-recency comparison with no required components.

editionLabel: IELLO / Hutter Trade German base rules, ©2016–2020; English summary
clarifications: That player receives the wire cutters and reveals a wire card belonging to another player. A player cannot cut their own wire.
The owner of the revealed card takes the next turn. At a new round, the last recipient of the cutters starts.
This answer covers Time Bomb Evolution's base rules, not the separate original Time Bomb game.
location: Spielaufbau step 6; Spielablauf; Rundenende; unnumbered final credits
